title: Atukula Burfi
description: A sweet, crispy burfi made with thick poha and grated jaggery, garnished with cashews and almonds.
instructions: Heat a pan and dry roast the poha for 5-6 minutes until very crispy.
Transfer the hot poha to a plate and immediately add the cashews on top.
Once cooled to room temperature, grind into a fine powder in a mixer jar.
Transfer the powder to a bowl, add grated jaggery, and mix well.
Gradually add milk and knead it like chapati dough until smooth.
Flatten the mixture onto a plate, cut into pieces, and garnish with almonds or cashews.

title: Vegetable Soup
description: A comforting, thick soup loaded with cabbage, carrots, capsicum, and spring onions, flavored with garlic and black pepper.
ingredients: 1/2 tbsp Corn flour (mixed with a little water)
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan. Add chopped garlic and ginger, and fry until light golden.
Add onions and lightly fry.
Add capsicum, carrot, and cabbage. Mix well on high flame.
Cover with a lid, reduce to low flame, and let it cook for 3 minutes.
Stir well, add water, and bring to a rolling boil until vegetables are soft.
Add salt to taste.
Mix corn flour with a little water in a small bowl, then pour it into the boiling soup to thicken.
Turn off the stove, add pepper powder, and garnish with spring onions.

title: Twisted Samosa
description: Deep-fried twisted samosas made with wheat flour and stuffed with a spiced mashed potato filling.
instructions: Sift wheat flour into a bowl, add salt, ajwain, and hot oil. Mix well. Add water and knead into chapati dough, cover and rest for 15 mins.
Mash boiled potatoes in a bowl, add all dry spice powders, salt, and corn flour, and mix well.
Roll out the dough into a chapati.
Apply the aloo curry evenly over it, place another rolled chapati on top, and press the edges with a little water to seal.
Cut into 4 pieces, twist them, and deep fry until golden.
Serve hot with tomato ketchup.

title: Masala Toast Sandwich
description: Mumbai-style toasted sandwich filled with a spicy potato and vegetable curry, served with cheese and green chutney.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add chopped onions and fry until transparent.
Add ginger, capsicum, and tomato, and fry well.
Add cooked sweet corn, green peas, mashed potatoes, and all dry spices (jeera, garam masala, chilli powder, pepper, turmeric, salt).
Mix everything into a thick curry and set aside.
Toast bread slices on both sides with ghee or butter in a pan.
Spread ketchup or green chutney on the bread. Add the curry filling (and optional cheese), top with another bread slice, and serve.

title: Green Chutney
description: A zesty and fresh dip made with fresh coriander, mint, ginger, and a bright kick of lemon juice.
instructions: Wash the coriander (including stems) and mint leaves thoroughly, and add to a mixer jar.
Add ginger, green chillies, black salt, and a pinch of turmeric.
Grind into a fine paste. Do not add too much water.
Add lemon juice and normal salt to taste, transfer to a bowl, and serve as a spread or dip.

title: Lemon Coriander Soup
description: A refreshing aromatic soup with sweet corn, carrots, capsicum, and fresh coriander.
instructions: Heat oil/butter in a pan. Add ginger garlic paste, chopped green chilli, capsicum, carrot, boiled sweet corn, and spring onions. Fry well.
Add 1.5 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Add aromatic powder and white pepper powder.
Mix corn flour with a little water, pour into the boiling soup, and stir until thickened.
Turn off the stove, add fresh coriander and lemon juice.

title: Bottle Gourd Soup
description: A healthy, smooth blended soup made with bottle gourd and garlic, seasoned lightly with jeera and pepper.
instructions: In a pressure cooker, add bottle gourd pieces, chopped onion, 1 clove of garlic, and 1 cup of water. Cook for 2-3 whistles. Let it cool.
Grind the cooked mixture into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a pan, add jeera and remaining garlic cloves.
Add the ground paste, another 1 cup of water, salt, and pepper powder. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam that forms.
Garnish with coriander and turn off the heat.

title: Hot and Sour Soup
description: A classic Indo-Chinese soup packed with veggies, mushrooms, soya sauce, and a spicy-sour kick from vinegar and chilli sauce.
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan, add finely chopped green chillies and fry.
Add cabbage, beans, carrot, mushrooms, and baby corn. Fry on high flame for 5-8 mins.
Add 500ml water and bring to a boil. Add dark soya sauce, sugar, white pepper, black pepper, and red chilli sauce. Boil for 5 mins.
Mix corn flour with water to milk consistency and pour it into the boiling soup to thicken.
Turn off the stove, add vinegar/lemon juice and garnish with spring onions.

title: Sweet Corn Chaat
description: A buttery, spicy street-style chaat made with boiled sweet corn, onions, tomatoes, and chat masala.
instructions: Boil sweet corn in a cooker for 4 whistles with a little salt and water, then drain.
Heat butter in a pan, add the boiled sweet corn, and roast lightly. Transfer to a mixing bowl.
Add finely chopped onion, tomato, red chilli powder, chat masala, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Add lemon juice, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve immediately.

title: Rava Dhokla
description: A soft, spongy steamed snack made from semolina, tempered with mustard seeds, sesame, and curry leaves.
ingredients: Tempering: 1 tbsp Oil, 1 tsp Mustard seeds, 4 slit Green chillies, 1 tsp White sesame seeds, Curry leaves, Coriander, Pinch of Hing
instructions: In a bowl, mix Sooji, curd, and water to make a batter. Add ginger-green chilli paste, sugar, and salt. Mix well and rest for 15-20 mins.
Heat oil in a pan, shallow fry jeera, grated carrot, and chopped capsicum, then add to the batter along with boiled sweet corn.
Adjust batter consistency with water if too tight, then mix in Eno/Cooking soda with 1 tsp water.
Grease an idli or dhokla plate, pour batter (leave half space for it to rise), and steam for 15-20 mins.
Test with a fork; if clean, remove and let cool before cutting into pieces.
Prepare tempering: heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, slit green chillies, sesame seeds, and hing. Pour over the cut dhokla. Garnish with coriander.

title: Spinach Soup
description: An immunity-boosting, iron-rich creamy soup made with fresh spinach, garlic, and whole spices.
instructions: Boil 1 liter of water. Blanch spinach leaves in boiling water for 3 mins, then immediately transfer to cold water.
Grind blanched spinach leaves, ginger, garlic, jeera, and green chilli into a smooth paste.
Heat a pan, add 1 tsp wheat/jowar flour and dry roast.
Add the spinach paste and mix well on medium flame. Add 500ml water, salt, cloves, cardamom, biryani leaf, and cinnamon.
Boil for 4 mins until it thickens slightly. Strain if desired and serve hot.

title: Bread Sticks
description: Crispy shallow-fried bread sticks coated in a spiced potato and sooji batter, topped with cheese.
ingredients: 1/4 tsp Turmeric, 1/2 tsp Chilli powder, 1/2 tsp Chat Masala, 1/2 tsp Garam Masala, 1/2 tsp Coriander powder
1/3 cup Sooji rava & 1/3 cup Maida/Wheat flour
instructions: In a bowl, mix all spice powders, finely chopped onions, and mashed potatoes to make a thick curry.
In another bowl, mix Sooji, Maida/Wheat flour, salt, chilli powder, crushed ajwain, and water to make a bajji-like batter.
Cut the edges off the bread slices.
Spread the potato curry evenly over a bread slice and cut into cubes or sticks.
Dip the coated bread sticks into the sooji batter.
Shallow fry in a pan on all 4 sides until crispy. Garnish with grated cheese and chilli flakes.

title: Tomato Soup
description: A rich, classic tomato soup enhanced with beetroot for deep color, flavored with biryani leaf and served with bread croutons.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp Black pepper & 1/2 tsp Garam masala
instructions: Heat butter in a pan, add chopped garlic, onions, and biryani leaf. Fry until the raw smell disappears.
Add beetroot pieces and fry briefly. Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 2-3 mins.
Add salt and sugar, mix well, and add 1 glass of water. Boil until tomatoes are very soft.
Turn off the stove, remove the biryani leaf, and let it cool. Grind into a smooth puree and strain it.
Heat another pan, add the strained puree, garam masala, jeera powder, black pepper powder, and salt. Boil until thick.
Serve hot with fresh cream and shallow-fried bread croutons.

title: Crispy French Fries
description: Homemade crispy fries coated in corn flour and tossed in a special garlic, oregano, and chat masala spice mix.
ingredients: 2 medium size Potatoes (60% cooked and grated/mashed)
Seasoning mix: 1 tsp Salt, 1 tsp Jeera powder, 1/2 tsp Chat masala, 1/2 tsp Oregano, 1/2 tsp Garlic powder
instructions: Mix the grated/mashed semi-cooked potatoes with corn flour, chat masala, and salt. Knead into a chapati-like dough (do not add water).
Keep it in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Take it out, roll it into a 1/2 inch thick flat shape, and cut into fry shapes.
Deep fry or shallow fry until crispy.
Mix all the seasoning ingredients together and sprinkle over the hot fries.

title: Macaroni Kurkure
description: A crunchy, deep-fried snack made from boiled macaroni coated in corn flour and spices.
ingredients: Spice mix: 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli, 1/2 tsp Jeera powder, 1 tsp Chat masala, 1/2 tsp Amchur powder, 1/2 tsp Pepper powder, 1/4 tsp Garam masala, 1/4 tsp Garlic powder, 1/2 tsp Black salt, 1/4 tsp Aromatic powder
instructions: Boil macaroni until soft but not broken. Drain hot water, rinse with cold water, and spread on a plate to dry slightly.
Coat the boiled macaroni evenly with salt, corn flour, maida, and a pinch of pepper powder.
Deep fry in hot oil until very crispy.
In a small bowl, mix all the ingredients for the spice mix.
Toss the hot, fried macaroni in the spice mix until well coated.

title: Ragi Soup
description: A highly nutritious, warm soup thickened with ragi flour, featuring crunchy beans, carrots, and spring onions.
instructions: Heat butter in a pan. Add chopped onions and fry.
Add chopped garlic, beans, carrot, and spring onions, and sauté well.
Add 1.5 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Mix ragi flour with a little water in a cup to avoid lumps. Pour the ragi mixture into the boiling soup and stir continuously.
Add pepper powder, salt, and aromatic powder.
Turn off the stove, garnish with fresh coriander, and squeeze a few drops of lemon juice before serving.

title: Beetroot Soup
description: A vibrant, beautiful soup made from beetroot, onions, and garlic, gently spiced with whole peppercorns.
instructions: Heat butter in a pressure cooker. Sauté ginger, onion, and garlic.
Add biryani leaf, black peppercorns, and jeera, and fry well.
Add chopped beetroot and carrot pieces. Fry thoroughly, then add 1.5 cups of water.
Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles. Let it cool to room temperature.
Remove the biryani leaf and peppercorns, then transfer to a mixer jar and grind into a smooth paste.
Strain the puree with an additional 1/2 cup of water.
Heat the strained liquid in a pan, bring to a boil, and thicken with corn flour mixed with water. Season with salt.
Serve hot garnished with coriander and spring onions.
